title: Pricing + packaging update for Dedicated throughput tiers (guardrails, exceptions, enablement)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
## Context
Dedicated customers have asked for predictable throughput commitments, but we currently have inconsistent language and inconsistent pricing anchors across: sales proposals, fleet costs/shapes, and runtime enforcement semantics.

This issue covers the **pricing + packaging** workstream for the new Dedicated throughput tiers (Standard / Performance / Premium) and ensures:
- Tier price points map cleanly to fleet costs + margin targets
- Discounting and exception requests have an explicit policy
- Order forms / MSA addenda are consistent with the throughput measurement standard and SLO definition
- Sales / CS have a usable cheatsheet + FAQ for launch

## Goals
1) Publish pricing guidance by tier (list prices + ranges) aligned with finance-approved unit economics.
2) Define discount + exception guardrails, with a lightweight approval workflow.
3) Align contract/SLA language references to the measurement standard and carve-outs.
4) Produce sales enablement artifacts (one-pager + FAQ) that are consistent with what SRE/runtime will actually enforce.

## Non-goals
- Finalizing every regional GPU supply constraint (handled in shape catalog + infra availability docs; this ticket only needs the packaging implications).
- Custom per-customer performance engagements or bespoke kernel tuning (separate perf engagements).

## Deliverables
- Confluence: Pricing model write-up
  - `sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-throughput-pricing-model.json`
- Confluence: Published tier definitions (pricing + packaging section must match)
  - `sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-tier-definitions.json`
- Sales enablement cheatsheet (tiers + qualifying + objections + exceptions)
  - `sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pricing-guidance/dedicated-throughput-tiers-cheatsheet.json`
- Internal FAQ updates for Support/CS/Sales
  - `sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/product-ops/throughput-slo-and-tiers-internal-faq.json`
- Contract references and order form insert language alignment (via PM-491)
  - `sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/dedicated-throughput-slo-contract-language.json`

## Proposed pricing/packaging direction (v1)
**Pricing basis:** reserved Dedicated capacity priced as a function of GPU type/count + control-plane overhead + included support/SLA package, with tier-based uplift for:
- stricter throughput objective (higher minimum sustained output tokens/sec)
- stricter overload policy (less tolerated throttling; higher provisioned headroom)
- reporting/SLO visibility + longer retention (where applicable)

**Packaging notes:**
- Tier eligibility is determined by both **shape** (fleet) and **policy** (burst/overload semantics).
- Any customer promise must reference the throughput measurement standard and explicitly state assumptions (prompt length distribution, streaming behavior, and excluded windows).

## Discount & exception guardrails (v1)
**Default discounting (pre-approved):**
- Up to X% on annual commit for Standard and Performance when term >= 12 months and customer accepts standard SLA.
- Premium requires explicit approval for any deviation from list due to supply scarcity + tighter headroom.

**Exceptions (must follow approval workflow):**
- Customer requests a throughput guarantee above published tier objective
- Customer requests unlimited burst (or burst outside published policy)
- Customer requests region/shape combination not in the supported matrix
- Customer requests remedies outside the standard credit schedule

**Approvals:**
- Pricing exception: Laura Bennett (Finance sponsor) + Rishi Malhotra (FP&A) + Lauren Bishop (Product)
- SLA/contract exception: Michael Grant (Legal) + Sofia Mendes (Commercial counsel)
- Supply/shape exception: Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz (Infra)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Finance sign-off on list price bands per tier and minimum floor pricing per shape.
- [x] Written discount guardrails + exception workflow published and shared with Sales Ops.
- [x] Sales cheatsheet finalized and reviewed by GTM sponsor (Jordan Blake) and enablement lead (Stephanie Nguyen).
- [x] Contract language (PM-491) references the same measurement standard and uses consistent definitions.
- [x] Launch deck/FAQ reflect the same promises (no off-menu commitments without approvals).

## Open questions (tracked here until closed)
1) Do we quote in tokens/sec, requests/sec, or both for sales-facing packaging?
   - Proposed: primary tokens/sec w/ a translation section (req/sec examples) by common workload profiles; ensure language is consistent with the SLO metric choice.
2) How do we handle mixed prompt sizes in a single commitment?
   - Proposed: commitment is based on the measurement standard’s normalization rules + explicit workload envelope; anything outside envelope is "best effort" and may be throttled.
3) Premium tier availability by region given GPU supply volatility?
   - Proposed: explicitly "limited availability" with quarterly review; do not sell Premium in constrained regions without infra approval.

## Notes / links
- Measurement standard: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/throughput-measurement-standard.json`
- Tier semantics + burst policy ADR: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0128-tiering-model-and-burst-policy.json`
- SLO contract language draft: `sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/dedicated-throughput-slo-contract-language.json`

## Rollout plan (pricing enablement)
1) Internal beta: publish cheatsheet + FAQ; enable Sales to quote tiers with "beta" rider.
2) Pilot customers: 2–3 accounts with explicit workload envelope and weekly reporting.
3) GA: remove beta rider, publish pricing guidance in sales collateral, enforce exception workflow.
